stories.title: World's Largest 'Glacial Archeology' Expedition Recovers 48 Stone Age Arrowheads and Shafts
stories.label: science
stories.summary: High in the mountains of southern Norway, a team of scientists has spent 20 years combing melting glaciers for traces of ancient life, and their latest haul is a treasure trove. They just pulled 48 arrowheads and shafts from the ice, some thousands of years old and made from different materials depending on the era. Each piece is like a little time capsule, giving historians new clues about how hunters lived and adapted over centuries. It's a wonderful reminder that our planet still has stories buried in it, just waiting to be found. No digging required, just patience and a bit of melting ice.
stories.why_good: A real discovery that happened, adds to human knowledge, no suffering involved, and is genuinely delightful and awe-inspiring.

stories.title: Daughter Gets to Join Dad as Co-Pilot, With Mom Serving on Flight's Cabin Crew
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A 22-year-old pilot named Zoë flew her very first flight as co-pilot sitting right next to her dad, who was the captain. To make the day even sweeter, her mom was working that same flight as part of the cabin crew. It happened on a KLM flight out of Amsterdam, and the whole family got to share this huge career milestone together in the sky. It's a lovely reminder of how dreams can run in families and come full circle in the most unexpected ways.
stories.why_good: A real, heartwarming family milestone that actually happened, with no suffering or controversy attached.
